$comment: The declared state of the Cloudflare zone (spec 040 §5.4, §12 step 4; TASK-100). `pnpm cloudflare:check` diffs the live zone against this file and never writes; `pnpm cloudflare:apply` writes the differences it can and reports `0 changes` on a second run. Parsed by `src/lib/cloudflare-zone.ts` (zod). Cache rules, the rate limit and DNS records are TASK-101's and are not in this file.

protocol.reason: Full (strict): Railway presents a valid certificate; anything less lets a MITM between Cloudflare and the origin
every http request is answered with a redirect to https, with HSTS from the origin in production only
TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are deprecated and no buyer needs them

the fastest handshake every current browser speaks. Cloudflare's values are `on`, `zrt` and `off`, and `zrt` is TLS 1.3 with 0-RTT (developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/additional-options/tls-13/). The two settings are one switch: writing `0rtt: on` turns this into `zrt`, and writing `on` here turns 0-RTT off, so `on` beside `0rtt: on` never settles (the founder's live apply, 2026-10-03). The schema refuses a pair that disagrees
0-RTT is applied to idempotent GETs only; POSTs (checkout, forms) are never replayed. It is the same switch as `tls_1_3: zrt` above
HTTP/2 is what lets LHCI move from `optimistic` to `median` (spec 040 §5.5)
faster connection setup on lossy mobile networks
spec 004 §14 A1's budget is measured in Brotli
costs nothing; it has no effect until the origin emits `Link` preload headers, which no task in spec 040 adds
it rewrites HTML, which breaks the ADR-0016 inline-script hash

doNotEnable.reason: rewrites and defers `<script>` elements: breaks the ADR-0016 inline hash and reorders the consent bootstrap
mutates the inline script's bytes, so the build-time sha256 no longer matches; Cloudflare deprecated it on 2024-08-05

checks.retired: Cloudflare deprecated Auto Minify on 2024-08-05 with no replacement

doNotEnable.reason: injects JavaScript into HTML (the same hash breakage) and mangles `mailto:` in the Impressum
image rewriting in the document; spec 006 owns the image pipeline and the LCP element must stay predictable

checks.retired: Cloudflare sunset Mirage in January 2026 with no replacement

doNotEnable.reason: blocks legitimate image fetches, including Googlebot Images; the other two Scrape Shield switches are the Email Address Obfuscation and Server-Side Excludes rows
spec 007 AC-12 requires `robots.txt` to be byte-exact and application-owned, with exactly one `Sitemap:` line

doNotEnable.feature: Bot Fight Mode / Super Bot Fight Mode
doNotEnable.reason: challenges Lighthouse, headless Playwright, legitimate crawlers and AI agents: the single most likely way to silently lose indexing. Super Bot Fight Mode is a paid-plan feature and cannot be on a free zone

doNotEnable.feature: AI Scrapers & Crawlers blocking / AI Labyrinth / pay-per-crawl; Search, Agent and Training set to Allow
doNotEnable.reason: founder direction 2026-09-16: AI agents may crawl this site. Pay-per-crawl is an account-level feature the zone token cannot read (TASK-100 escalation E-1)
interstitial HTML for every visitor; switched on by hand during an incident only, so `cloudflare:apply` reports it and never switches it off itself

doNotEnable.feature: IP-geolocation redirect rules; any use of `cf-ipcountry` to route
doNotEnable.checkedElsewhere: `fo/no-geo-redirect` fails the lint on any use in the code; the zone's rules are TASK-101's to declare and check

doNotEnable.reason: it would put an auth wall in front of the indexable site
doNotEnable.checkedElsewhere: spec 040 AC-25 / T-26 (a production document answers 200 with no auth header); Access policies are not readable with the zone token's scopes

doNotEnable.feature: Cloudflare Access / basic-auth on staging and PR
doNotEnable.reason: replaces Vercel Deployment Protection; plan/01 §10 keeps non-production password-protected. The default is the basic-auth check in `src/proxy.ts` (spec 040 §5.4)
doNotEnable.checkedElsewhere: spec 040 AC-25 / T-26 and the `preview` job's unauthenticated-401 assertion (AC-26)

doNotEnable.reason: the same hash argument; if one is ever needed it must not touch the document body
doNotEnable.checkedElsewhere: spec 040 AC-18 / T-18 (the body through Cloudflare is byte-identical to the origin's); Workers routes and Snippets are not readable with the zone token's scopes
